trainingNotice: 本站的阅读、听力、口语和写作任务均为原创衔接训练，不是 IELTS 官方真题，也不是完整模拟考试。练习正确率和自动检查不等于 IELTS 分数。第一册用于打基础，备考还需要更长篇幅、更复杂语言和真实考试条件下的专项训练。

sources.title: General Training Reading：官方考试结构
General Training Writing：官方考试结构
General Training 官方样题入口

facts.title: 先选对考试类别
facts.body: Academic 与 General Training 的听力、口语考试相同；阅读和写作不同。需要哪一种，应以接收成绩的机构要求为准。

facts.title: Listening · 约 30 分钟 / 40 题
facts.body: 4 个部分，每部分 10 题，录音只播放一次。前两个部分是生活场景，后两个部分是教育或培训场景。这里的短训练可重播用于学习，考试练习时应尝试只听一次。

facts.title: Academic Reading · 60 分钟 / 40 题
facts.body: 3 个部分，阅读并回答 40 题。正式考试文字量和难度高于本站短篇衔接练习；阅读时间包括作答时间。

facts.title: General Training Reading · 60 分钟 / 40 题
facts.body: 3 个部分：日常生活短文、工作相关材料，以及较长的一般兴趣文章。判断题要区分 FALSE（与原文矛盾）和 NOT GIVEN（原文信息不足），不能靠常识补答案。

facts.title: Academic Writing · 图表 + 议论文
facts.body: 总计 60 分钟，完成两项任务。Task 1 根据图表、表格或示意图写至少 150 词，建议约 20 分钟；Task 2 写至少 250 词，建议约 40 分钟。Task 2 的评分权重是 Task 1 的两倍。

facts.title: General Training Writing · 信件 + 议论文
facts.body: 总计 60 分钟。Task 1 为情境信件，至少 150 词；Task 2 为议论文，至少 250 词。建议分配 20 / 40 分钟，信件语气应符合对象和目的。

facts.title: Speaking · 11–14 分钟 / 3 部分
facts.body: Part 1 谈熟悉话题，约 4–5 分钟；Part 2 准备 1 分钟后作个人长回答，尽量持续到 2 分钟；Part 3 进一步讨论相关抽象问题，约 4–5 分钟。本站单题计时是练习安排，不是每个正式问题的固定时限。

facts.title: 总分怎样计算
facts.body: 听、说、读、写四科分数取平均，再取到最接近的半分。平均分尾数为 .25 时进到下一个半分，.75 时进到下一个整数分。

facts.title: 正确题数不能机械换分
facts.body: 听力与阅读每题答对得 1 分，再换算成 9 分制。换算门槛会随试卷略有变化；General Training 阅读达到同一分数通常需要答对更多题。本网站的 8 题短练习不换算 IELTS 分数。

facts.title: 写作：四个评分维度
facts.body: 任务完成或回应、连贯与衔接、词汇、语法范围与准确性；每项任务中四个维度权重相同。字数达标只是基本检查，不能证明观点展开或语言质量达标。

facts.title: 口语：四个评分维度
facts.body: 流利与连贯、词汇、语法范围与准确性、发音，四项权重相同。录音回听可帮助发现停顿和表达问题；语音转文字不能单独可靠评价发音或给出正式分数。

reading.title: More than a place to borrow books
reading.subtitle: 原创阅读衔接 · 8 题 · 建议 12 分钟
reading.instructions: 阅读 A–E 段并完成问题。TRUE 表示符合原文，FALSE 表示与原文矛盾，NOT GIVEN 表示原文没有足够信息。所有答案只依据本文。文中城镇和研究均为虚构教学情境。
reading.passage:
A. For many years, the public library in the fictional town of Westbridge was mainly a place to borrow books. When the council planned to renovate the building, it first asked residents what they needed. The most common request was for quiet study space, followed by reliable internet access. A larger café was suggested too, but it was not among the two leading requests.

B. The renovated library opened in March. It kept its book collection and added twelve study desks, six public computers and a small room for community classes. Library membership remained free. Visitors could use a computer for one hour without payment, but they had to book a session at the information desk. To help residents who worked during the day, the library began closing at eight on two evenings each week, rather than at six.

C. A volunteer team introduced weekly sessions on basic digital skills. Participants learned how to complete online forms, organise documents and recognise suspicious messages. The organisers originally expected most learners to be retired. In fact, nearly half of the people who joined the first month were employed adults. Some said that they used phones confidently but had little experience with computers. The volunteers therefore adjusted the lessons to include more keyboard practice.

D. Not every change was immediately successful. The class room was close to the study area, and some students complained about noise. Managers did not cancel the classes. Instead, they installed a door that reduced sound and moved group activities to less busy hours. A follow-up survey found fewer complaints, although several students still preferred to study early in the morning.

E. After six months, the library recorded more visits than in the same period of the previous year. However, the manager warned against treating visitor numbers as the only measure of success. A person might visit repeatedly because a computer task remained difficult. Staff also began asking whether users had completed their tasks and felt more confident. The council planned to review this feedback before deciding whether another neighbourhood should receive a similar facility.

questions.prompt: 1. What did residents request most often?
questions.explanation: A 段明确说最常见的要求是 quiet study space。不要把后面的 internet access 误作第一名。

questions.prompt: 2. Visitors had to pay for their first hour on a public computer.
questions.explanation: B 段说 one hour without payment，即一小时免费，与题目 had to pay 矛盾。

questions.prompt: 3. What was needed before using a public computer?
questions.explanation: B 段的 had to book a session at the information desk 直接给出使用条件。免费不代表无需预约。

questions.prompt: 4. The library stayed open until eight on two evenings each week.
questions.explanation: B 段末句写明 closing at eight on two evenings each week。

questions.prompt: 5. Why did volunteers add more keyboard practice?
options: Online forms were no longer available
questions.explanation: C 段：一些人会用手机，但 little experience with computers，因此增加键盘练习。

questions.prompt: 6. All of the volunteers had previously worked as teachers.
questions.explanation: C 段介绍志愿者的教学内容，没有交代他们以前的职业。不能从会教课推断全部当过老师。

questions.prompt: 7. The library cancelled its classes after students complained.
questions.explanation: D 段直接说 did not cancel the classes。解决方法是装门和调整活动时间。

questions.prompt: 8. What is the manager's main point in paragraph E?
options: Higher visitor numbers always prove success
Computers should replace the book collection
The council has already approved another library
Success should include whether users achieve their goals
questions.answer: Success should include whether users achieve their goals
questions.explanation: E 段不能只看访问次数，还问用户是否完成任务并增强信心。另建图书馆仍需评估，并未批准。

listening.title: Booking a community photography course
listening.subtitle: 原创听力衔接 · 8 题 · 建议先听一遍
listening.instructions: 先读题，再播放完整对话。训练信息纠正、日期、价格和条件。学习时可以重听；挑战时只听一遍，交卷后再看原文。合成朗读用于练习，不是官方考试录音。
listening.script:
Receptionist: Good morning, Riverside Community Centre. How can I help?
Caller: I'd like to join the beginner photography course. Is the next one on Saturday?
Receptionist: That was our original plan, but the tutor is unavailable. It now starts on Sunday, the fourteenth of June.
Caller: Sunday is fine. Does it begin at nine?
Receptionist: At nine thirty. Please arrive fifteen minutes earlier to register. The session finishes at twelve thirty.
Caller: And where should I go?
Receptionist: Room four, on the first floor. We normally use room two, but it's being painted. There is a lift beside reception.
Caller: How much does the course cost?
Receptionist: Forty pounds for all three sessions. The course booklet is included. You can pay by card when you register.
Caller: Do I need an expensive camera?
Receptionist: No. A phone camera is perfectly suitable. Please bring your own device because we cannot lend equipment.
Caller: Will we spend the whole morning inside?
Receptionist: No, there will be a short practice walk in the park. Bring a waterproof jacket in case it rains.
Caller: Can I cancel if my work schedule changes?
Receptionist: Yes. Contact us at least two days before the first session to receive a full refund.
Caller: Great. Could you reserve a place for me?
Receptionist: Certainly. May I have your name?

questions.prompt: 1. On which day will the course now start?
questions.explanation: 先提到原计划 Saturday，随后 now starts on Sunday 更正；听力要以最后确认的信息为准。
听到 the fourteenth of June，即 6 月 14 日。这里是虚构预约情境，没有指定年份。

questions.prompt: 3. At what time should participants arrive to register?
questions.explanation: 课程 9:30 开始，要求提前 15 分钟到达：9:30 − 0:15 = 9:15。题目问到达时间，不是上课时间。

questions.prompt: 4. Which room will the course use?
questions.explanation: 接待员确认 Room four。Room two 是平时用的房间，这次正在油漆。

questions.prompt: 5. What does the forty-pound fee cover?
questions.explanation: 费用是 for all three sessions，随后说明 booklet is included。设备不提供。

questions.prompt: 6. What photography equipment should the caller bring?
questions.explanation: 手机相机也可以，但要 bring your own device，中心不能外借设备。

questions.prompt: 7. Why should participants bring a waterproof jacket?
questions.explanation: 课程包含在公园的 practice walk，防水外套用于应对下雨。不是整场都在室内。

questions.prompt: 8. When must the caller contact the centre to receive a full refund?
options: At least two days before the first session
On the morning of the first session
questions.answer: At least two days before the first session
questions.explanation: 原文条件为 at least two days before the first session，注意 at least（至少）和 first（第一节）。

speaking.prompt: Do you work or study? What do you enjoy about it?
tips: 先直接回答，再用一个具体细节说明。
可以说 I work as… / What I enjoy most is…，但不要只念模板。
录音后检查主谓一致、时态和是否回答了两个问题。

speaking.prompt: How do you usually spend your evenings? Has this changed recently?
tips: 用一般现在时讲通常习惯，再用过去时或现在完成时讲变化。
给一个真实例子，比罗列许多活动更清楚。
这是本站练习时限，正式 Part 1 每题没有统一固定秒数。

speaking.prompt: Describe a skill you would like to improve. Say what it is, why it matters to you, how you plan to practise it, and explain what progress would look like for you.
tips: 准备时只写关键词：技能、原因、方法、可见进步。
用一个个人经历支撑原因，把计划说具体。
尽量说到 2 分钟；不会某个词时换一种表达，避免整段停住。

speaking.prompt: Describe a public place that you enjoy visiting. Say where it is, what you do there, who you usually go with, and explain why it is important to you.
tips: 选真实而熟悉的地方，如图书馆、公园或运动场。
用一次具体经历延长回答，并说明感受。
地点描述不是目标本身，最后要回答为什么重要。

speaking.prompt: What are the advantages and disadvantages of learning a new skill online rather than in a classroom?
tips: 先概括，再各讲一个优点和缺点，并提供例子。
可以比较灵活性、反馈速度和自我管理，但要解释因果。
不要把所有学习者一概而论；可以用 for some learners / depending on the subject。

speaking.prompt: How should a city decide which public facilities deserve more funding?
tips: 给一个可解释的标准，如需求、可达性或维护成本。
用一个具体设施说明标准如何应用。
补充一种权衡：使用人数少的服务是否也可能重要？

writing.title: Academic Task 1 · 公共设施使用数据
writing.prompt: The table shows the number of visits to four public facilities in the fictional town of Brookfield in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Figures count visits, not individual visitors. The data are fictional and provided for this original practice task.
writing.dataTitle: Brookfield public facility visits, 2025 · 单位：次
checklist: 写出清楚的总体概述，而不只是逐项报数。
最高、最低和主要差距是否准确？
数据是访问次数，不是不同居民人数；没有人口覆盖率。
只有一个年份，不推断增长趋势或原因。
至少 150 词，使用连贯段落，检查比较级和数词。
writing.sample:
The table compares the number of visits to four public facilities in the fictional town of Brookfield in 2025. The facilities together recorded 100,000 visits during that year.

Overall, public parks attracted the largest number of visits, while the community hall was the least frequently visited facility. Parks and the library together accounted for three quarters of all recorded visits, substantially more than the other two facilities combined.

Public parks received 45,000 visits, representing 45 percent of the total. This figure was 15,000 higher than that for the library, which recorded 30,000 visits and contributed a further 30 percent. The sports centre ranked third with 20,000 visits. Its total was two thirds of the figure for the library and less than half the number recorded for parks.

By comparison, the community hall had only 5,000 visits, equivalent to 5 percent of the overall total. The sports centre received four times as many visits as the hall, while the corresponding figure for parks was nine times as high. The gap between the most and least visited facilities was therefore 40,000 visits.
writing.sampleNotice: 原创参考写法，用于比较结构和数据表达；未经官方考官评分。不要背诵为通用答案。

writing.title: General Training Task 1 · 调整课程安排
writing.prompt: You have enrolled in an evening course at a community centre, but your work schedule has changed. Write a letter to the course coordinator. Explain the change in your circumstances, describe how it affects your attendance, and ask about a suitable alternative arrangement. You do not need to write any addresses. Begin your letter: Dear Sir or Madam,
checklist: 开头是否清楚说明写信目的？
三个要求都覆盖：情况变化、出勤影响、替代安排。
对不熟悉的协调员使用礼貌、正式的语气。
请求足够具体，让收件人可以回应。
结尾与 Dear Sir or Madam 匹配，可用 Yours faithfully。
至少 150 词；检查时态、日期关系和完整段落。
writing.sample:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about the beginner photography course that I joined earlier this month. I would like to ask whether it would be possible to change my class because my working hours have recently been revised.

My employer has asked me to work until eight o'clock on Tuesdays for the next six weeks. Unfortunately, this is the evening when my photography class meets, so I will be unable to attend the remaining sessions in my current group. I have enjoyed the two lessons I have already completed and would very much like to continue learning.

Could you please let me know whether there is a weekend group with available places? I am free on both Saturday and Sunday mornings. If a transfer is not possible, I would be grateful if you could explain whether I may join the next course instead. Please also tell me if either arrangement would involve an additional fee.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to hearing which option would be suitable.

Yours faithfully,
Alex Chen
writing.sampleNotice: 原创参考信件，未经过官方评分。学习其任务覆盖与语气，不要机械套用。

writing.title: Task 2 · 公共图书馆仍然重要吗？
writing.prompt: Some people believe that public libraries are no longer necessary because information is available online. Others think libraries still provide essential services. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. This is an original practice task suitable for essay preparation in both test categories.
checklist: 讨论了双方观点，并明确给出自己的立场。
每个主体段有中心论点、解释和具体例子。
例子不冒充没有查证的研究或统计。
回应的是公共图书馆是否仍有必要，不偏成泛谈互联网。
检查代词指代、句间逻辑和不必要的重复。
至少 250 词，预留约 5 分钟检查；字数不是分数。
writing.sample:
As more information becomes available online, some people argue that public libraries have lost their purpose. Others believe that these institutions continue to meet important community needs. Although digital resources have reduced the need to visit a library for certain tasks, I believe libraries remain valuable when their services reflect local needs.

The argument against maintaining traditional libraries is understandable. A reader can now find news, reference materials and many books without leaving home. Online searches are also convenient for people who work irregular hours and cannot visit a building during its opening times. From this perspective, spending public money on shelves of rarely used books may seem less useful than improving internet access. If a library offers nothing beyond materials that residents can easily obtain elsewhere, its role deserves to be reconsidered.

However, access to information involves more than the existence of a website. Some residents do not own a suitable computer, while others need help judging whether information is reliable. A library can provide both equipment and support. It can also offer a quiet place to study, which may be especially important for students living in crowded homes. For example, a learner preparing for a professional qualification may need a desk and several hours without interruption, even if all the course materials are digital.

In my view, the strongest solution is to adapt libraries rather than remove them. Local authorities should assess which services residents actually use and where important needs remain unmet. A combination of books, digital assistance and accessible study space can make a library useful to people with different circumstances.

In conclusion, online information has changed the function of libraries, but it has not eliminated the need for them. Continued funding is justified when libraries provide practical services that residents cannot readily obtain elsewhere.
writing.sampleNotice: 原创参考文章，展示双边讨论与明确立场；不宣称任何 IELTS 分数。
